idiom_name: typed async enrich function + Required<Pick<...>> enriched contract
implementation_notes: Same runtime idiom as JavaScript, but the enrichment contract is expressed in the type system: declare the wire shape with optional fields and an enriched shape that makes them required (Msg & Required<Pick<Msg, 'customerName' | 'region'>>), so downstream code cannot compile while it might receive an unenriched message. The lookup sits behind a CustomerSource interface that tests replace, and framework hooks such as NestJS interceptors or queue-consumer middleware provide the insertion point when the application already has one; the interceptor form returns next.handle().pipe(map(...)) with the enriched value.
pitfalls: The enriched type is an assertion, not a guarantee: if the resource can return partial data you must narrow or throw, otherwise the type lies to every consumer.
Required<Pick<...>> on the wire type hides the fact that the producer may still send those fields - document who wins on collision.
An interceptor or middleware that awaits the resource inside the request path adds latency to every call it is bound to; scope it to the routes that need enrichment.
